body:
The four changes from your computer are adopted on the web, with three small bugs fixed on the way. A web step now shows on your board what it is doing, like a step on your computer: the line is sent with each update the step already makes, so it moves every few minutes rather than every 15 seconds. You see it in the board once the board's page is refreshed to this version.

### What each change costs (measured here, in characters)

| Command | Characters | Note |
|---|---|---|
| resume, as a part | 15425 | the largest parts: what the train found so far 4890, how a part works 3353, lessons 2434; the pieces add 696 |
| form | 150 | once at turn 1 |
| done | 683 | here with an unfilled form; it refuses an open piece |
| sub | 73 | one line of JSON per tick |
| permission-mode | 4 | "auto" here |
| commands | 226 | a topic: 235 |

The live line costs no model call and nothing in context on the web: the hook is silent; the document rides in the push the step already makes (one more write in its batch).

### Review of the four commits, bug by bug

1. **A product name was refused as a file name.** The new check on what you read first refused "Node.js" (and Vue.js, Next.js...) as if it were a file, and since it is now an error, not a note, a step could not end. Fixed: common product names pass; a real file name is still refused. Tested.
2. **Two pieces could get the same number.** When a piece without a number came before one with a number, both became piece 1, so ticking "1" hit the wrong one. Fixed: an unnumbered piece takes a number nobody holds. Tested.
3. **The help line for ticking a piece still showed the old form** (title only). It now says by number, and that dropping a piece the task names needs a reason.
4. **A test assumed it did not run as root.** On the web every session is root, and Claude Code refuses the bypass mode as root, so the kit rightly says auto: the test now fakes a normal user, and checks the root case too.

Checked and fine: the loop breaker (said once, at the 8th identical call), the hook that finds the project from a subfolder, the installer moving the old default to the new one once, the page tests closing their browser.

Seen, not changed (small): the live line's first look at pieces can skip a file changed before the session's first command; two pieces of a task list that has two numbered lists (1 to 3, then 1 to 2) are read as prose, by design.

### The live line on the web: how it works now

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[web step's command] --> B[its hook: what it does now]
  B --> C[the container's copy of the board]
  C -->|each push the step already makes| D[the Artifact board]
  D --> E[the page: line under the step]
```

- The hook now runs in web sessions too (it already ran here, by accident, because this repository is installed for the computer; now it is declared for both).
- A web step launched with "You are part ... --role part --post ..." is now recognized as a part (before, only the kit's own launch words were): its hook found this step at once.
- The push sends the line as one more document, created the first time and pinned to its version after that; it is never counted as unsent, so the Stop check does not nag about it.
- The page reads the line on the board that holds the step (an attached board like this one); before, it looked at the main board's place and would have shown nothing. The page test plants a wrong-board line and proves it is not shown.

### What a web session sees of permission-mode

- It prints "auto" here: the session runs as root, and Claude Code refuses the bypass mode as root; nothing is recorded as accepted either.
- On the web the mode is not taken from the kit at all: a web part is started by the orchestrator's session tool, which gives it the orchestrator's own mode; the kit's choice only applies to sessions it starts on a computer. Nothing in the web flow needs a change. The welcome text that still said "auto" now says what the mode is.

The loop breaker and the live line were not run on a computer here (no computer attached); their tests ran.
Why the page's phone checks fail on the web (folding a train at 411 px): same failure before the four changes; left for its own step.
